page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne-c14d3.14xlarge is a storage-dense instance type belonging to the big data server family. Operating on the x86_64 architecture and the KVM hypervisor, it is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 56 dedicated virtual CPUs accompanied by 160.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 2.86 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This instance does not include GPU acceleration.

Storage capacity is the primary hardware focus of this instance, featuring 70,866 GB of integrated local HDD storage. Network throughput is scaled to support massive data movements, offering a 35 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, targeting internal cluster deployments and virtual private cloud network topologies.

The combination of 56 vCPUs with over 70 TB of spinning disk storage provides high cost efficiency for bulk data storage and sequential read/write operations. However, because local storage relies on mechanical disks rather than solid-state drives, random IOPS throughput is inherently restricted. This hardware profile is appropriate for distributed big data processing, Apache Hadoop or Spark clusters, central log aggregation systems, data lakes, and high-volume batch ETL pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne-c14d3.14xlarge is a dedicated big data instance designed for high-capacity local data processing and retention. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz across 56 dedicated vCPUs, paired with 160.0 GB of memory (2.86 GB per core). A key attribute of this server is its integration of 70,866 GB of local HDD storage alongside a 35 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, managed via the KVM hypervisor. It contains no GPU accelerators. The use of dense mechanical storage offers strong cost efficiency for bulk sequential data storage, though random IOPS performance is lower compared to NVMe flash media. Consequently, the instance is tailored for big data distributed computing platforms, Apache Hadoop nodes, large-scale log analysis, archival storage, and batch ETL workloads.
